record.paper_title: A Survey on Offline Reinforcement Learning: Taxonomy, Review, and Open Problems
record.original_question: Which data-collection strategies and data-processing methods can produce more exploratory offline datasets and make better use of unlabeled data, so that offline reinforcement learning becomes effective in a broader range of real-world domains rather than only in settings with narrowly curated logged data?

evidence.quote: Although a lot of focus has been placed on the development of new algorithms, these works show how the data we use to train these algorithms can be just as important for their performance. Finding new exploratory techniques to collect the data and novel ways to leverage unlabeled data can help extend offline RL’s applicability to even more real-world domains.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the offline reinforcement learning setting: an agent must learn a policy π maximizing expected discounted return in a Markov decision process M = (S, A, P, r, γ) using only a fixed, previously collected dataset D = {(s_i, a_i, r_i, s'_i)} of transitions, with no further environment interaction allowed during training. Empirically, offline RL algorithms perform well when D is sufficiently diverse and broadly covers the state–action space, but degrade sharply when D is narrowly curated (e.g., generated by a single near-optimal or single suboptimal behavior policy with limited coverage). In addition, in many real-world applications one has access to large quantities of auxiliary "unlabeled" trajectories U = {(s_j, a_j, s'_j)} that lack reward annotations.

Problem: Identify and characterize
(a) data-collection strategies (i.e., procedures or behavior policies, possibly adaptive, possibly using intrinsic motivation, ensembles, mixtures of policies, or human/expert priors) that produce offline datasets D with provably or empirically better coverage and exploratory properties for downstream offline RL; and
(b) data-processing and learning methods that incorporate unlabeled, reward-free transition data U together with a smaller labeled dataset D to improve the learned policy's performance and generalization,
such that the resulting offline RL pipeline yields effective policies across a broad range of real-world domains rather than only on settings with narrowly curated logged data. Provide algorithmic constructions and supporting theoretical guarantees (e.g., sample-complexity or suboptimality bounds in terms of coverage coefficients of D ∪ U) or rigorous empirical evidence.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a broad, open research direction in offline RL. Recent work (e.g., reward-free pretraining, UDS / PDS for unlabeled data sharing, exploratory data collection methods like APT, ProtoRL, ExORL benchmarks) has made partial progress, but no comprehensive solution exists. The problem remains an active open area as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Don't Change the Algorithm, Change the Data: Exploratory Data for Offline RL (ExORL)
status_evidence.snippet: Shows that simple offline RL algorithms trained on exploratory data can match SOTA, indicating data collection strategy is critical; partial progress, not a complete solution.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on exploratory data collection for offline RL.

status_evidence.title: How to Leverage Unlabeled Data in Offline RL (UDS / PDS)
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes labeling unlabeled trajectories with zero reward (UDS) and provides analysis showing benefits under coverage assumptions; partial answer to unlabeled-data usage.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on incorporating unlabeled data into offline RL.
